text: The epic now blocks on all 28 of its children, and each child is attached to the epic by a parent-child edge. br and bv both treat parent-child as blocking, and br marks every child of a blocked parent as blocked. The epic stays blocked while any child is open, so no child can ever become ready, and br close refuses to close any of them without --force. The result is a deadlock: on the plan subgraph there are 34 cycles that run through these edges. Simulating the readiness queue with br's rules leaves 34 of 88 beads never ready: the epic, all 28 children, jev-1yqu, jev-grzn, jev-r1vp, jev-uzq1 and the mission root jev-q3q8. bv agrees: in a scratch copy with the gate closed, b35c.1 (the 2nd-highest PageRank bead) is not actionable and is shown as blocked by jev-b35c. The edges come from round 3's own L5 fix (r3 L5-GraphR3.jsonl:11, 'Add blocking edges from jev-b35c to its open children'). That fix was wrong, and I am demoting it here.
evidence: beads_rust src/storage/sqlite.rs:1559-1571 (blocks edges on non-closed beads -> blocked_issues_cache), :1650-1708 (children whose parent-child parent is in the cache are added to it; it is transitive), :1285-1287 (br ready excludes cached ids), src/cli/commands/close.rs:221-240 (close refuses a blocked issue unless --force). Snapshot: jev-b35c dependencies = blocks on jev-b35c.1..28 + g57u; each jev-b35c.N has parent-child -> jev-b35c (diff r3->r4: 'DEP blocks jev-b35c + [28 children]'; jev-b35c comment 2026-10-04T23:58:28Z 'the epic now blocks on all 27 non-closed children'). var/agent-tmp/L5r4.graph/graph.py: cycles_blocks=[] but cycles_blocks+parent_child=34 (e.g. jev-b35c -> jev-b35c.1 -> jev-b35c); sim_br_semantics steps 54/88, never_ready 34 (graph.json). bv on the snapshot: blockers_to_clear lists jev-b35c.15 blocked_by [jev-b35c, ...] and jev-b35c.3 blocked_by [jev-b35c, jev-b35c.1]; g57u 'unblocks 24' leaves out b35c.1/.23/.24/.25, which block only on g57u. Scratch copy var/agent-tmp/L5r4.graph/sim-gate-closed (g57u set closed): bv actionable 25, top_picks [acs2, 06wt, j0er], b35c.1 absent. var/agent-tmp/L5r4.graph/sim-fix (same, with the 28 epic->child blocks edges removed): actionable 30, top_picks [acs2, b35c.1, 06wt]. br-semantics sim after that removal: 88/88 reach ready, never_ready [].
fix: Remove all 28 blocking edges jev-b35c -> jev-b35c.N (`br dep remove jev-b35c jev-b35c.N` for N=1..28). Any epic->child blocking edge is a cycle with that child's parent-child edge, so none can be kept. Do not defer the epic either, because a deferred parent blocks its children (sqlite.rs:1610-1648). The closure rule stays: jev-q3q8 already blocks on every non-dropped child, and the epic closes through `br epic close-eligible` once all parent-child children are closed, followed by its `classifier overview --json` check. Add a planted negative to jev-q3q8 acceptance 3 or bead-lint: an epic with a blocking edge to its own child fails lint.

text: This bead builds what its own family bead refuted. N4 says blocking an identical bash retry would be wrong 76% of the time (245/321 identical retries succeeded) and puts 'block identical bash retry' on D9's no-build list. N4 also records the Jev Choice retry-vs-fix design as refuted (R142: .444 vs majority .556). N4.1 is that hook: it blocks the retry, and Jev's Choice picks the fix. Its reference labels come from paid gpt-5-mini via OpenRouter. The general-LLM arm (b35c.15) refuses anything that is neither an OpenRouter :free id nor a local model. Jev's own answers also fill any rows the reference skips, so the scored model labels itself.

A worker would claim X2 and then stall on the missing gateway, or call :8010 directly, which the bead forbids. But X2 does not block on the conformance harness, and it commits no recorded Clef answers.
